subject: Coffee & Tea
title: What Is Extraction?
description: A quick, practical guide to What Is Extraction?.

hook.text: Brewing coffee is dissolving soluble compounds out of ground beans. That process is called extraction.

buildup.text: Coffee grounds contain about 30% soluble material. A good brew extracts 18–22% of it.

discovery.text: Under-extracted coffee tastes sour and thin. Over-extracted coffee tastes bitter and harsh.

twist.text: Different compounds extract at different rates. Acids come first, sugars next, bitter compounds last.

climax.text: Great coffee hits the sweet spot: enough acids for brightness, enough sugars for sweetness, minimal bitterness.

punchline.text: Too little is sour. Too much is bitter. Perfection is between.

quiz.question: What percentage of solubles should a good brew extract?

details.summary: Extraction is the process of dissolving flavor compounds from ground coffee into water. About 30 percent of coffee is soluble, but the ideal extraction range is 18 to 22 percent. Under-extraction produces sour, thin coffee while over-extraction tastes bitter and harsh.
details.whyItMatters: Extraction is the core science of brewing. Controlling it is the difference between a balanced, delicious cup and a disappointing one.
takeaways: Ideal extraction falls between 18 and 22 percent of soluble mass
Under-extraction tastes sour; over-extraction tastes bitter
Grind size, time, and temperature control extraction rate

faq.question: How can you tell if coffee is under or over extracted?
faq.answer: Under-extracted coffee tastes sour, salty, thin, and lacks sweetness. Over-extracted coffee is bitter, astringent, dry, and hollow. Well-extracted coffee is sweet, balanced, and has a pleasant lingering finish.

faq.question: What variables control extraction?
faq.answer: Grind size is the most powerful lever: finer grinds extract faster. Water temperature, brew time, agitation, and the coffee-to-water ratio also play major roles. Adjusting any one of these changes the extraction percentage.
